fix.pr_body:
## What was wrong

The submenu popover (visible on 901–1600px wide screens when hovering a menu item) appeared and disappeared instantly via a `display: none` ↔ `display: block` toggle. CSS cannot transition `display`, so there was no ease animation.

The existing medium-width media query also redundantly set `top: 0; position: absolute` on the hover rule, which are already present on the base `.submenu` selector.

## What changed

Inside the `@media only screen and (min-width: 901px) and (max-width: 1600px)` block in `shared_web/static/css/pd.css`:

- Added a default-state rule `nav li > .item + .submenu` that overrides `display: none` with `display: block`, sets `opacity: 0; pointer-events: none` (visually hidden and non-interactive), and declares `transition: opacity 0.2s ease`.
- Changed the hover rule `nav li:hover > .item + .submenu` to set `opacity: 1; pointer-events: auto` (fades in, becomes interactive).
- Removed the now-redundant `top: 0; position: absolute` from the hover rule (already on the base `.submenu` rule).

This gives a smooth 200ms ease fade when the submenu appears and disappears. Using opacity+pointer-events instead of display avoids both the instant snap and any border-flicker that would occur with a width transition.

## How it was validated

- `uv run --frozen python dev.py lint` — passed ("All checks passed!").
- Unit tests were not run; the change is CSS-only with no Python logic touched, making a unit-test run not applicable.

Fixes #12664
fix.pr_title: Add opacity ease transition to medium-width submenu popover (#12664)

This sidesteps the 'border disappearing during ease' issue the author noted (which was likely caused by transitioning width or display). Changes confined to pd.css, ~10-15 lines.
